title: A fixed GJ 674 orbit cuts error by 6.4 percent in 32 sparse-year HARPS exposures, but noise tests depend on leverage
abstract: An exact orbit fitted to 224 GJ 674 HARPS exposures predicts higher harmonics in 32 omitted sparse-year exposures. The frozen prediction reduces weighted squared error by 6.43 percent. Ten controls and seven leave-year-out checks keep positive point gains. Raw residual sign tests give tail fractions of 0.021-0.044. Scaling residuals for fit leverage raises these to 0.111-0.126. The sparse test has only 16 residual degrees of freedom. Thus it does not give robust evidence for the higher harmonics. This extends the earlier dense-season test to disjoint exposures from the same instrument. No new planet or independent instrument confirmation is established. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included; external data stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Frozen higher-harmonic gains in 32 omitted exposures and conditional noise tests. HC2 scales residuals for fit leverage. Gains are point estimates, not confidence intervals.
